mainTopic: Why the משנה lists grain-containing items, and which תנא (רבי מאיר or רבי אליעזר) holds that mixtures of חמץ and נוקשה carry only a לאו
overview: The amud opens by finishing the explanation of the women's hair-removing paste in the משנה. Poor girls used lime, wealthy girls used סולת, and princesses used שמן המור, which is either myrrh oil or oil from unripe olives. A ברייתא of רבי יהושע explains that the משנה lists specific items, even though 'כל שהוא ממין דגן' covers them, so that people learn their names. A story about a visitor who avoided כותח shows why this matters. The גמרא then asks which תנא holds that the listed items carry only a לאו (באזהרה). רב יהודה says רבי מאיר, using a ברייתא about שיאור. רב נחמן says רבי אליעזר, who gives a לאו for a mixture of חמץ. Each אמורא explains why he rejects the other's view, and a ברייתא supports רב יהודה. Finally, the גמרא searches for רבי אליעזר's source in the פסוקים, settling on the word 'כל'. Its defense of that source, about including women, continues on the next amud.

steps.title: Different hair-removing pastes for different classes of girls
steps.stepSummary: Girls who matured physically before reaching legal age used a paste to remove body hair. Poor girls used lime, wealthy girls used fine flour (סולת), and princesses used שמן המור, as the פסוק in אסתר says.
steps.simpleTranslation: [Girls] who reached physical maturity but had not yet reached the age: daughters of the poor would smear them with lime, daughters of the wealthy would smear them with fine flour, and daughters of kings with שמן המור, as it says: 'Six months with שמן המור.'
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא is finishing its explanation of the women's paste mentioned in the משנה. It describes which kind of paste each social class used.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The point of interest for פסח is the middle case. Wealthy girls used סולת, which is a grain product, so this paste contains חמץ material. That is why it appears in the משנה's list. The פסוק from מגילת אסתר shows that royalty used something more luxurious, שמן המור, which the next steps define.

keyTerms.meaning: their physical maturity (signs of adulthood)
smear / plaster (apply a paste)
lime (a mineral powder)
fine wheat flour
a luxurious cosmetic oil mentioned in אסתר

steps.confusionAlert: This amud starts in the middle of a sentence. The words 'girls who reached maturity' continue a statement that began on the previous lines. They explain the משנה's טיפולי נשים (women's paste).

phrases.english: who reached their physical maturity,
but had not yet reached the age (of majority),
daughters of the poor — they smear them with lime,
daughters of the wealthy — they smear them with fine flour,
phrases.notes: This is the grain-based paste relevant to חמץ.

phrases.english: daughters of kings — with shemen hamor,
as it is stated:
'Six months with shemen hamor' (Esther 2:12).

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Continues the explanation (begun on the previous amud) of the משנה's טיפולי נשים.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Wealthy girls' hair-removing paste was made of סולת. That grain content is why it appears among the משנה's חמץ items.

steps.title: What is שמן המור?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks what exactly שמן המור is.
steps.simpleTranslation: What is 'שמן המור'?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא asks for a definition of the term from the פסוק. It is setting up the two answers that come next.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The phrase שמן המור is unclear. It could be a special perfume or a type of oil. The גמרא wants to identify the substance precisely.

keyTerms.meaning: what is?

phrases.english: What is 'shemen hamor'?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Asks for the meaning of a term quoted in Step 1.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: The identity of the substance called שמן המור.

steps.title: First answer: it is סטכת
steps.stepSummary: רב הונא בר ירמיה says that שמן המור is סטכת, a type of perfumed oil (myrrh oil).
steps.simpleTranslation: רב הונא בר ירמיה says: סטכת.
steps.whatsHappening: רב הונא בר ירמיה gives the first definition: שמן המור is a substance called סטכת.
steps.deeperAnalysis: סטכת is generally understood as oil of myrrh, a fragrant luxury product. On this view, שמן המור is named for the actual myrrh plant.

keyTerms.meaning: setaket — myrrh oil / a fragrant resin oil

phrases.english: Rav Huna bar Yirmeya says:
phrases.notes: The Sefaria translation reads 'רב הונא בר חייא'. The source text here reads בר ירמיה.

phrases.english: Setaket (myrrh oil).

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the question of Step 2.

steps.title: Second answer: oil from unripe olives
steps.stepSummary: רב ירמיה בר אבא says that שמן המור is olive oil made from olives that have not yet reached a third of their growth.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב ירמיה בר אבא said: Olive oil that has not reached a third [of its ripening].
steps.whatsHappening: A second אמורא gives a different definition. He says שמן המור is oil pressed from very unripe olives.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Oil from very young olives is sharp and acidic. That makes it effective at removing hair. This explains why princesses would use it as a depilatory, just as others used lime or flour.

keyTerms.meaning: olive oil
a third (of the fruit's ripening)

phrases.english: Rav Yirmeya bar Abba said:
olive oil that has not reached a third (of its growth).

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Offers an alternative answer to Step 2's question, differing from Step 3.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: שמן המור = oil from olives less than a third ripe.

steps.title: A ברייתא supports the unripe-olive-oil view
steps.stepSummary: A ברייתא quotes רבי יהודה: אנפיקנין is olive oil from olives less than a third ripe. People smear it on because it removes hair and softens the skin.
steps.simpleTranslation: It was taught: רבי יהודה says: Anpiknin is olive oil that has not reached a third. And why do they smear it? Because it removes the hair and softens the skin.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings a ברייתא that describes the same unripe olive oil. This backs up רב ירמיה בר אבא's definition.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רבי יהודה confirms that oil from olives less than a third ripe was a known product, called אנפיקנין. He also says it was used as a hair remover and skin softener. This fits exactly the role of שמן המור in the princesses' beauty treatment, so it supports רב ירמיה בר אבא.

keyTerms.meaning: it was taught in a ברייתא
oil from unripe olives (omphacine)
makes fall out / removes (hair)
softens / pampers

phrases.english: It was taught: Rabbi Yehuda says:
anpiknin —
is olive oil that has not reached a third,
and why do they smear it on?
because it removes the hair
and softens the skin.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Supports Step 4's definition with a תנאי source.
steps.raayaObject: רב ירמיה בר אבא's view that שמן המור is oil from olives less than a third ripe, used for hair removal.
steps.raayaSupportSource: ברייתא of רבי יהודה about אנפיקנין.
steps.whatToRemember: שמן המור is either myrrh oil (סטכת) or a hair-removing oil from very unripe olives. A ברייתא confirms that such unripe-olive oil was used to remove hair and soften skin.

steps.title: Quoting the משנה's general rule
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא quotes the משנה's closing rule: anything made from a type of grain falls under the prohibition.
steps.simpleTranslation: [The משנה says:] This is the principle: anything that is from a type of grain.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא quotes the next line of the משנה. It is setting up a discussion about why the משנה needed a list at all.
steps.deeperAnalysis: After listing many specific items, the משנה gives a general rule. Anything containing grain is included in the prohibition of owning חמץ on פסח. This rule will prompt the question in the next step.

keyTerms.meaning: this is the general principle
a type of grain (the five grains)

phrases.english: This is the principle:
anything that is from a type of grain.

steps.triggerLanguage: זֶה הַכְּלָל כׇּל שֶׁהוּא מִמִּין דָּגָן
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Moves on from the definition of the cosmetic items to the משנה's concluding principle.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Anything made from one of the grains is included in the prohibition on פסח.

steps.title: Why list items if a general rule covers them?
steps.stepSummary: A ברייתא quotes רבי יהושע: if the general rule already includes anything made of grain, why did the חכמים list these specific items?
steps.simpleTranslation: It was taught: רבי יהושע said: Since we have learned that anything that is a type of grain — one transgresses with it on פסח, why did the חכמים list these?
steps.whatsHappening: רבי יהושע points out that the general rule seems to make the list unnecessary. He asks why the list is there.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Usually a general rule makes a detailed list redundant. If every grain product is forbidden, naming individual items adds no new law. So there must be a different purpose for the list.

keyTerms.meaning: transgresses (the prohibition)
they listed / counted

phrases.english: It was taught: Rabbi Yehoshua said:
Now, since we have learned
that anything that is a type of grain —
one transgresses with it on Passover,
why did the Sages list these items?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Questions the need for the list, given the rule quoted in Step 6.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: The purpose of the משנה's detailed list when a general rule already exists.

steps.title: So people become familiar with these items
steps.stepSummary: The list exists so that people become familiar with these items and their names. That way they know these products contain grain.
steps.simpleTranslation: So that one should be familiar with them and with their names.
steps.whatsHappening: The ברייתא answers: the list is educational. It teaches people to recognize these products as grain-containing.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Many of these items, such as cosmetics, dyes, and dips, do not obviously contain grain. Without the list, people would not realize they own חמץ. So the list adds no new law, but it gives practical awareness.

keyTerms.meaning: familiar / accustomed
their names

phrases.english: so that one will be familiar with them
and with their names.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers רבי יהושע's question from Step 7.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: The list is educational: it makes people aware that these products contain grain.
steps.whatToRemember: The משנה's list does not add new law beyond 'כל שהוא ממין דגן'. It teaches people to recognize less obvious products that contain grain.
steps.whyThisMatters: This shows a principle of how משניות teach. Sometimes a detailed list is there for practical awareness, not to create new halacha.

steps.title: The visitor who stopped eating when he heard the word כותח
steps.stepSummary: A man from ארץ ישראל visiting בבל was eating meat. He asked for a dip. When he heard his hosts call it כותח, he stopped eating, because he knew כותח contains milk.
steps.simpleTranslation: This is like the case of a man from the West (ארץ ישראל) who came to בבל. He had meat with him. He said to them: 'Bring me a dip.' He heard them saying: 'Bring him כותח.' As soon as he heard 'כותח,' he stopped eating.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא tells a real-life story to show why it is useful to know the names of foods.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Step 8 said the חכמים listed specific foods so people would learn their names and know what is inside them. Here the visitor did not recognize the dip by sight. But because he knew the name כותח, he realized it had milk in it and avoided eating it with meat. Knowing a food's name protected him from an איסור.

keyTerms.meaning: A man from the West, meaning from ארץ ישראל (which lies west of בבל)
Happened to come / visited
A dip or relish to eat bread with
A Babylonian dip made with milk (and bread crusts and salt)
He withdrew / stopped eating

steps.whyThisMatters: It turns the principle from Step 8 into a practical lesson: knowing a food's name tells you its ingredients, even when you cannot recognize the food itself.

phrases.english: Like this case of a certain man from the West (Eretz Yisrael)
who came to Babylonia,
he had meat with him,
He said to them: Bring me a dip.
phrases.notes: He wanted something to dip his bread in while eating his meat.

phrases.english: He heard them saying: Bring him kutach.
Once he heard 'kutach', he stopped eating.
phrases.notes: He knew כותח contains milk, which may not be eaten with meat.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Shows the reason given in Step 8 working in a real story
steps.raayaObject: Step 8's claim that the list in the משנה teaches people the names of foods so they know what the foods contain
steps.raayaSupportSource: The story of the visitor from ארץ ישראל who avoided כותח because he knew its name

steps.title: Quoting the משנה: these carry only a warning prohibition
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא quotes the next phrase of the משנה. It says the listed items are 'באזהרה', meaning they carry a לאו but not כרת.
steps.simpleTranslation: The משנה says: 'These are under a warning prohibition.'
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא quotes a new phrase from the משנה to set up its next question.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The items in the משנה are not punished with כרת like ordinary חמץ. They fall only under a warning (לאו). The גמרא is about to ask which תנא holds this.

keyTerms.meaning: These (items)
A warning prohibition, meaning a לאו, not כרת

steps.confusionAlert: 'באזהרה' does not mean the items are permitted. It means they are forbidden by a לאו, but the punishment of כרת does not apply.

phrases.english: These are under a warning prohibition.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Moves on to a new phrase in the משנה
steps.mimraCoreRuling: The listed items carry a לאו (warning prohibition), not כרת.

steps.title: Which תנא holds this view?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks which תנא holds two things. First, real grain חמץ that is only part of a mixture carries a לאו. Second, נוקשה on its own also carries a לאו.
steps.simpleTranslation: Who is the תנא who holds that real grain חמץ in a mixture, and נוקשה (hardened חמץ) in its pure form, are both under a לאו?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא asks whose opinion the משנה follows when it says these items are 'באזהרה'.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The משנה's list contains two kinds of items. Some are real חמץ mixed into something else, like כותח. Others are נוקשה, a weak, inferior חמץ that is unmixed, like the glue of scribes. The גמרא wants a תנא who puts both kinds under a לאו, and not every תנא agrees about this.

keyTerms.meaning: Who is the תנא (whose view is this)?
Real, full חמץ made from grain
Through a mixture (mixed into another food)
Hardened, inferior חמץ that is not fit to eat normally
In its own pure form, unmixed

phrases.english: Who is the tanna

phrases.aramaic: דְּחָמֵץ דָּגָן גָּמוּר עַל יְדֵי תַּעֲרוֹבוֹת,
phrases.english: who holds that full grain leaven in a mixture,
and hardened leaven in its pure form, are under a prohibition (lav)?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Asks whose opinion the משנה phrase quoted in Step 10 follows
steps.sheelahInformationSought: Which תנא puts both real חמץ in a mixture and unmixed נוקשה under a לאו

steps.title: The answer: it is רבי מאיר
steps.stepSummary: רב יהודה, quoting רב, answers that the משנה follows רבי מאיר.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב יהודה said in the name of רב: It is רבי מאיר.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא names the תנא behind the משנה. The proof comes in the next step.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רב identifies רבי מאיר as the one who holds that these items carry a לאו. The claim still needs a source, so the גמרא brings a ברייתא next.

keyTerms.meaning: רב יהודה quoting his teacher רב

phrases.english: Rav Yehuda said that Rav said:
It is Rabbi Meir,

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the question of Step 11

steps.title: The proof from the ברייתא about שיאור
steps.stepSummary: A ברייתא teaches that שיאור (half-leavened dough) must be burned or given to a dog, and a person who eats it receives forty lashes. Lashes are the punishment for a לאו.
steps.simpleTranslation: As it was taught in a ברייתא: שיאור must be burned, or a person may give it to his dog. And one who eats it receives forty lashes.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings a ברייתא to prove that רבי מאיר holds נוקשה carries a לאו.
steps.deeperAnalysis: שיאור is dough that has only started to rise, so it counts as נוקשה. The punishment for eating it is forty lashes (מלקות), which is the punishment for a לאו, not כרת. This shows that נוקשה carries a לאו in the view of this ברייתא. The ברייתא itself does not name רבי מאיר; the גמרא shows in Step 16 that the forty-lashes clause follows רבי מאיר.

keyTerms.meaning: As it was taught (in a ברייתא)
Dough that has only begun to rise (half-leavened), a type of נוקשה
It must be burned
With forty, meaning forty lashes (מלקות), the punishment for a לאו

steps.confusionAlert: Forty lashes does not mean the item is real חמץ with כרת. Lashes are the punishment for a plain לאו, and that is exactly the point of the proof.
steps.whatToRemember: According to רב, the משנה's rule that these items are only 'באזהרה' (a לאו without כרת) follows רבי מאיר. The proof is a ברייתא in which eating שיאור, a form of נוקשה, earns forty lashes.

phrases.english: as it was taught: Leavening dough must be burned,
or he gives it to his dog,
and one who eats it is punished with forty lashes.
phrases.notes: Lashes are the punishment for a לאו, so this shows that שיאור (a form of נוקשה) carries a לאו.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Supplies the source for רב's answer in Step 12
steps.raayaObject: רב's claim that the משנה follows רבי מאיר
steps.raayaSupportSource: The ברייתא about שיאור, where eating it brings forty lashes (a לאו)

steps.title: The ברייתא seems to contradict itself
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא points out that the ברייתא about שיאור seems to contradict itself. 'It must be burned' implies benefit is forbidden, but 'give it to his dog' implies benefit is allowed.
steps.simpleTranslation: This ברייתא itself is difficult! You said 'שיאור must be burned', so it seems benefit from it is forbidden. Then the ברייתא teaches 'or he gives it to his dog', so it seems benefit from it is allowed!
steps.whatsHappening: Before using the ברייתא as a proof, the גמרא stops to ask a question about the ברייתא itself. Two of its rulings seem to clash.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Requiring burning only makes sense if you are not allowed to get any use or benefit from the item. Feeding it to your own dog is a kind of benefit, so it would only be allowed if benefit is permitted. The same ברייתא cannot seemingly say both things about the same food.

keyTerms.meaning: This itself is difficult. The source has a problem within itself.
A prohibition against getting any benefit or use from an item, not just against eating it
Apparently / this shows that
His dog

steps.confusionAlert: This question is not attacking רב's claim that the משנה follows רבי מאיר. It is only pointing out an inner problem in the ברייתא that must be fixed before the ברייתא can work as a proof.

phrases.english: This itself is difficult:
phrases.notes: The ברייתא from Step 13 has an internal problem.

phrases.english: you said 'שיאור must be burned',
apparently it is forbidden for benefit,
and then it teaches: 'or he gives it to his dog',
apparently it is permitted for benefit!

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges the internal consistency of the ברייתא quoted as proof in Step 13.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: 'Burn it' implies אסור בהנאה, while 'give it to the dog' implies מותר בהנאה. These are contradictory rulings about the same item.

steps.title: Each clause refers to a different definition of שיאור
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא explains that the clauses refer to different definitions. 'Burn it' refers to each תנא's own שיאור, according to his own view. 'Give it to the dog' refers to רבי מאיר's שיאור, but according to רבי יהודה.
steps.simpleTranslation: This is what the ברייתא means. 'שיאור must be burned' refers either to רבי מאיר's שיאור according to רבי מאיר, or to רבי יהודה's שיאור according to רבי יהודה. 'He gives it to his dog' refers to the dough that רבי מאיר calls שיאור, but according to רבי יהודה.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers the contradiction. The two clauses are not talking about the same dough according to the same opinion.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רבי מאיר and רבי יהודה disagree about which stage of rising counts as 'שיאור'. Each one says that what he himself calls שיאור is forbidden for benefit and must be burned. רבי יהודה, however, holds that the earlier-stage dough that רבי מאיר calls שיאור is only like נוקשה and is permitted for benefit, so it may be given to a dog.

keyTerms.meaning: This is what it means. The גמרא is reinterpreting the source.
Dough that has started to rise but is not fully חמץ. Its exact definition is disputed.
A תנא who holds a stricter view about partly-risen dough
A תנא who defines שיאור as a later stage and is more lenient about earlier stages

steps.confusionAlert: 'דרבי מאיר לרבי יהודה' does not mean רבי מאיר is speaking to רבי יהודה. It means 'the dough that רבי מאיר calls שיאור, judged by רבי יהודה's view.'

phrases.english: This is what it is saying:
'שיאור must be burned' means:
the שיאור of רבי מאיר, according to רבי מאיר,
phrases.notes: Dough that רבי מאיר defines as שיאור is forbidden for benefit in his view.

phrases.english: or the שיאור of רבי יהודה, according to רבי יהודה.
'And he gives it to his dog' means:
the שיאור of רבי מאיר, according to רבי יהודה.
phrases.notes: For רבי יהודה this earlier-stage dough is permitted for benefit.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the internal contradiction raised in Step 14.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Splitting the ברייתא's clauses between different definitions and different תנאים
steps.terutzHavaAmina: Both clauses speak about the same dough according to the same view, which would be a contradiction.
steps.terutzMaskana: 'Burn it' follows each תנא's own definition. 'Give it to the dog' is רבי מאיר's שיאור judged by רבי יהודה.

steps.title: The forty-lashes clause follows רבי מאיר
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא finishes its explanation of the ברייתא. The final clause, that one who eats it gets forty lashes, returns to רבי מאיר's view.
steps.simpleTranslation: And 'one who eats it gets forty lashes': here we have come back to רבי מאיר.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא completes its explanation of the ברייתא. It assigns the last clause, about lashes, to רבי מאיר.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רבי יהודה treats this dough as permitted for benefit, but רבי מאיר holds that eating it brings forty lashes, meaning it carries a לאו. This is the clause the גמרא needs for its proof about רבי מאיר.

keyTerms.meaning: Forty lashes, the punishment for transgressing a לאו
We have come back to / now we are at the view of

phrases.english: And 'one who eats it receives forty lashes' —
we have come back to רבי מאיר.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Completes the clause-by-clause explanation begun in Step 15.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Assigning the final clause to a specific תנא
steps.terutzMaskana: The lashes clause reflects רבי מאיר's view that this kind of dough carries a לאו.

steps.title: Proof that the משנה follows רבי מאיר
steps.stepSummary: With the ברייתא now explained, the גמרא concludes that רבי מאיר holds plain נוקשה carries a לאו. All the more so, real חמץ in a mixture carries a לאו. These are exactly the two points asked about in Step 11.
steps.simpleTranslation: We have learned that according to רבי מאיר, נוקשה on its own carries a לאו. All the more so, full grain חמץ that is part of a mixture carries a לאו.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא wraps up the proof. It shows that רבי מאיר is the תנא who holds both rules the משנה needed.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The ברייתא showed that רבי מאיר gives lashes for weak, partly-leavened dough eaten by itself. The גמרא reasons with a קל וחומר: if even weak חמץ carries a לאו, then real, strong חמץ certainly does, even when it is mixed into something else. This confirms רב's statement that the משנה follows רבי מאיר.

keyTerms.meaning: We have heard / learned that he holds
Hardened, weak חמץ that is not fully leavened
In its own pure form, not mixed into anything
All the more so (a קל וחומר)
A mixture

steps.whatToRemember: According to רבי מאיר, both נוקשה by itself and real חמץ in a mixture carry a לאו, but not כרת. That is why רב said the משנה, which calls these items 'באזהרה', follows רבי מאיר.
steps.whyThisMatters: This closes the loop opened in Steps 11 and 12. The משנה's ruling of 'באזהרה' for both kinds of items is now tied to a known תנא.

phrases.english: We have learned that רבי מאיר holds
נוקשה in its pure form is under a לאו.
And all the more so full grain חמץ
phrases.notes: This is a קל וחומר from the weaker case to the stronger one.

phrases.english: that is in a mixture.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Uses the now-explained ברייתא to complete the proof for רב's answer in Step 12.
steps.maskanaFinalTakeaway: רבי מאיר holds that נוקשה by itself carries a לאו, and by קל וחומר so does real חמץ in a mixture. Therefore the משנה follows רבי מאיר.

steps.title: רב נחמן says the משנה follows רבי אליעזר
steps.stepSummary: רב נחמן gives a different author for the משנה, רבי אליעזר. He brings a ברייתא where רבי אליעזר says real חמץ gets כרת and its mixture gets a לאו, while the חכמים say a mixture gets nothing at all.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב נחמן said: The משנה follows רבי אליעזר. A ברייתא teaches: For eating real grain חמץ, one is punished with כרת. For eating its mixture, one violates a לאו. These are the words of רבי אליעזר. The חכמים say: For real grain חמץ, one is punished with כרת. For its mixture, there is no punishment at all.
steps.whatsHappening: A second אמורא, רב נחמן, offers a different answer to the question of whose view the משנה follows. He says it is רבי אליעזר and quotes a ברייתא to show it.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רב יהודה pointed to רבי מאיר. רב נחמן instead points to רבי אליעזר, who explicitly gives a לאו for a mixture that contains real חמץ. The חכמים disagree and say a mixture carries no punishment at all.

keyTerms.meaning: Real, fully leavened grain חמץ
Punished with כרת, being cut off spiritually (the severe punishment)
Its mixture, meaning חמץ mixed into other food
As it was taught in a ברייתא
With nothing, meaning no punishment at all

steps.confusionAlert: Do not mix up the two levels of punishment. כרת is for real חמץ by itself, and everyone agrees on that. The argument is only about a mixture: רבי אליעזר says it carries a לאו, and the חכמים say it carries nothing.

phrases.english: Rav Nachman said:
It (the Mishnah) is Rabbi Eliezer,
as it was taught (in a baraita):

phrases.aramaic: עַל חָמֵץ דָּגָן גָּמוּר — עָנוּשׁ כָּרֵת,
phrases.english: For full-fledged grain leaven, one is punished with karet;
for its mixture, one violates a prohibition (lav).
These are the words of Rabbi Eliezer.
And the Sages say:

phrases.aramaic: עַל חָמֵץ דָּגָן גָּמוּר — עָנוּשׁ כָּרֵת,
phrases.english: For full-fledged grain leaven, one is punished with karet;
for its mixture, there is nothing (no punishment).

steps.triggerLanguage: רַב נַחְמָן אָמַר: רַבִּי אֱלִיעֶזֶר הִיא, דְּתַנְיָא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Offers a second author for the משנה, as an alternative to רב יהודה's רבי מאיר.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: The משנה follows רבי אליעזר, who holds that a mixture containing real חמץ carries a לאו.

steps.title: רבי אליעזר covers both points of the משנה
steps.stepSummary: From the ברייתא, רבי אליעזר holds that real חמץ in a mixture carries a לאו. All the more so, pure נוקשה carries a לאו.
steps.simpleTranslation: We hear from רבי אליעזר that real grain חמץ in a mixture carries a לאו. All the more so, נוקשה by itself carries a לאו.
steps.whatsHappening: רב נחמן finishes his proof. He shows that רבי אליעזר's view matches both points the משנה needs.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The ברייתא directly gives the first point: real חמץ in a mixture carries a לאו. The second point comes from a קל וחומר. If even diluted real חמץ gets a לאו, then undiluted נוקשה surely gets one too.

keyTerms.meaning: A mixture
All the more so (a קל וחומר)
In its own form, pure and unmixed
We have heard him say, meaning we know his view

steps.whatToRemember: רב נחמן's answer covers both points of the משנה through רבי אליעזר. Real חמץ in a mixture gets a לאו, as stated directly in the ברייתא. Pure נוקשה gets a לאו through a קל וחומר.

phrases.english: And we have heard Rabbi Eliezer, who said

phrases.aramaic: חָמֵץ דָּגָן גָּמוּר עַל יְדֵי תַּעֲרוֹבֶת — בְּלָאו,
phrases.english: that full-fledged grain leaven in a mixture carries a prohibition (lav),
and all the more so hardened leaven in its pure form.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Draws the conclusion from the ברייתא quoted in Step 18.
steps.maskanaFinalTakeaway: רבי אליעזר holds that both real חמץ in a mixture and pure נוקשה carry a לאו, so he fits the משנה.

steps.title: Why did רב נחמן not agree with רב יהודה?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks why רב נחמן did not simply say, like רב יהודה, that the משנה follows רבי מאיר.
steps.simpleTranslation: And רב נחמן, what is his reason for not saying like רב יהודה?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא compares the two answers. It asks why רב נחמן needed a new author when רב יהודה had already found one.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רב יהודה's answer seemed to work, since Step 17 showed that רבי מאיר covers both points. So the גמרא wants to know what weakness רב נחמן saw in it.

keyTerms.meaning: What is the reason?
Did not say like, meaning did not agree with

phrases.english: And Rav Nachman,

phrases.aramaic: מַאי טַעְמָא לָא אָמַר כְּרַב יְהוּדָה?
phrases.english: what is the reason he did not say like Rav Yehuda?

steps.triggerLanguage: וְרַב נַחְמָן, מַאי טַעְמָא לָא אָמַר כְּרַב יְהוּדָה
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Now that there are two answers, the גמרא asks why רב נחמן rejected the first one.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: What flaw did רב נחמן find in attributing the משנה to רבי מאיר?

steps.title: רבי מאיר may only speak about pure hardened leaven
steps.stepSummary: רב נחמן would answer that רבי מאיר may give a לאו only for pure נוקשה. Real חמץ in a mixture might carry כרת according to him, so the קל וחומר of Step 17 fails.
steps.simpleTranslation: He would say to you: Perhaps רבי מאיר only said there that pure נוקשה carries a לאו. But real grain חמץ in a mixture, no. It might carry more than a לאו.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא explains רב נחמן's reasoning. He doubts that רבי מאיר's ruling about pure נוקשה tells us anything about a mixture of real חמץ.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Step 17 reasoned that if weak נוקשה gets a לאו, then real חמץ in a mixture surely gets at least a לאו. רב נחמן suggests that real חמץ, even when mixed, may be strong enough to carry כרת. The משנה treats a mixture as only a לאו, so it would not match רבי מאיר.

keyTerms.meaning: He would say to you
Perhaps
He only said it up to here, meaning his ruling applies only in that case
There, meaning in the earlier source

steps.confusionAlert: רב נחמן is not saying that a mixture is more lenient for רבי מאיר. He is saying it might be stricter, carrying כרת. That is why the משנה, which gives only a לאו, would not fit רבי מאיר.

phrases.english: He would say to you:

phrases.aramaic: דִּילְמָא עַד כָּאן לָא קָאָמַר רַבִּי מֵאִיר הָתָם
phrases.english: Perhaps Rabbi Meir only said it there
regarding hardened leaven in its pure form;

phrases.aramaic: אֲבָל חָמֵץ דָּגָן גָּמוּר עַל יְדֵי תַּעֲרוֹבֶת — לָא.
phrases.english: but full-fledged grain leaven in a mixture, no (it may be karet).

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר לָךְ: דִּילְמָא עַד כָּאן לָא קָאָמַר רַבִּי מֵאִיר הָתָם
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the question of Step 20 by attacking the קל וחומר of Step 17.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: The קל וחומר from נוקשה to real חמץ in a mixture fails. Real חמץ in a mixture may carry כרת according to רבי מאיר.
steps.whyThisMatters: This shows why a קל וחומר can fail. Being 'stronger' could mean a bigger punishment, not just the same לאו.

steps.title: Why did רב יהודה not agree with רב נחמן?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks the opposite question: why did רב יהודה not say that the משנה follows רבי אליעזר? The next step answers this.
steps.simpleTranslation: And רב יהודה, what is his reason for not saying like רב נחמן?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא sets up its next move by asking why רב יהודה rejected רב נחמן's clear proof from רבי אליעזר. The answer will follow.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רב נחמן's source is explicit: רבי אליעזר directly gives a לאו for a mixture. So the גמרא wants to know what flaw רב יהודה found in it.

keyTerms.meaning: The אמורא who said the משנה follows רבי מאיר
The אמורא who said the משנה follows רבי אליעזר

phrases.english: And Rav Yehuda,

phrases.aramaic: מַאי טַעְמָא לָא אָמַר כְּרַב נַחְמָן?
phrases.english: what is the reason he did not say like Rav Nachman?

steps.triggerLanguage: וְרַב יְהוּדָה מַאי טַעְמָא לָא אָמַר כְּרַב נַחְמָן
steps.relationToPreviousStep: The reverse of the Step 20 question, now aimed at רב יהודה.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: What flaw did רב יהודה find in attributing the משנה to רבי אליעזר?

steps.title: רב יהודה: רבי אליעזר only spoke about real חמץ in a mixture
steps.stepSummary: רב יהודה would answer that רבי אליעזר gave a לאו only for real grain חמץ mixed into something else. He never said anything about pure נוקשה, so the משנה cannot be pinned on him.
steps.simpleTranslation: He would say to you: רבי אליעזר only spoke there about real grain חמץ that is part of a mixture. About hardened חמץ on its own, he said nothing.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers the question from Step 22. It explains why רב יהודה did not say the משנה follows רבי אליעזר.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רב נחמן built a קל וחומר: if a mixture of real חמץ gets a לאו, then pure נוקשה surely does. רב יהודה rejects that קל וחומר. Real חמץ is a stronger kind of חמץ, even when it is diluted. Weak חמץ (נוקשה) may be a totally different category that רבי אליעזר permits completely.

keyTerms.meaning: 'Until here he only said' — limits a rabbi's statement to the exact case he spoke about
Full, real חמץ made from grain
A mixture
Hardened (weak) חמץ on its own, not mixed with anything

steps.confusionAlert: There are two different ways to be a 'weaker' kind of חמץ. One is real חמץ that is diluted in a mixture. The other is pure חמץ that never fully leavened (נוקשה). רב יהודה says a rule about the first case tells you nothing about the second.

phrases.english: He would say to you:

phrases.aramaic: עַד כָּאן לָא קָאָמַר רַבִּי אֱלִיעֶזֶר הָתָם
phrases.english: Rabbi Eliezer only said there
about full-fledged grain chametz
in a mixture.
But hardened chametz in its pure form —
he did not say.

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר לָךְ: עַד כָּאן לָא קָאָמַר רַבִּי אֱלִיעֶזֶר הָתָם
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the question posed in Step 22
steps.sheelahInformationSought: Why רב יהודה did not attribute the משנה to רבי אליעזר
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: רבי אליעזר only spoke about a mixture of real חמץ. He may not prohibit pure נוקשה at all, so the קל וחומר of Step 19 is not reliable.

steps.title: A ברייתא supports רב יהודה: mixtures get a לאו, not כרת
steps.stepSummary: A ברייתא learns from 'כל מחמצת' that four foreign foods containing חמץ are prohibited. It then learns from 'כי כל אכל חמץ ונכרתה' that only real חמץ gets כרת, while its mixture gets only a לאו.
steps.simpleTranslation: A ברייתא supports רב יהודה. The פסוק 'You shall eat nothing leavened' comes to include Babylonian כותח, Median beer, Edomite vinegar and Egyptian זיתום. You might think eating these gets כרת. So the פסוק says 'For whoever eats חמץ will be cut off.' This teaches that real grain חמץ gets כרת, and its mixture gets a לאו.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings a ברייתא that backs up רב יהודה. The proof itself is spelled out in the next step.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The ברייתא only lists foods that are mixtures containing real חמץ. It gives them a לאו and not כרת. It never mentions any pure נוקשה item. That missing piece is what the גמרא will build on.

keyTerms.meaning: A ברייתא was taught that supports his view
To include (something extra learned from a פסוק)
Babylonian dip made with moldy bread crusts, milk and salt — a mixture containing חמץ
Spiritual cutting-off, the severe punishment for eating real חמץ on פסח
'The verse teaches' — introduces the פסוק that settles the question
Its mixture

phrases.english: It was taught in accordance with Rav Yehuda:
"You shall eat nothing leavened" —
to include Babylonian kutach
and Median beer
and Edomite vinegar and Egyptian zitom.
Might one think he is punished with karet?
The verse teaches:
"For whoever eats leaven... shall be cut off",

phrases.aramaic: עַל חָמֵץ דָּגָן גָּמוּר — עָנוּשׁ כָּרֵת,
phrases.english: for full grain chametz — he is punished with karet,
and for its mixture — a prohibition (lav).

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Brings textual support for רב יהודה after his answer in Step 23
steps.raayaObject: רב יהודה's view that the משנה follows רבי מאיר and not רבי אליעזר
steps.raayaSupportSource: A ברייתא that lists only mixtures of real חמץ and assigns them a לאו

steps.title: The ברייתא is רבי אליעזר, and he does not prohibit pure נוקשה
steps.stepSummary: Only רבי אליעזר gives a לאו for a mixture, so the ברייתא follows him. Since it leaves out pure נוקשה, רבי אליעזר does not prohibit נוקשה.
steps.simpleTranslation: Who have we heard say that a mixture gets a לאו? רבי אליעזר. Yet the ברייתא does not mention pure נוקשה. Learn from this that רבי אליעזר does not hold that נוקשה is prohibited.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא explains how the ברייתא proves רב יהודה's point.
steps.deeperAnalysis: In Step 18, the חכמים said a mixture gets nothing at all. So a source that gives a mixture a לאו must be רבי אליעזר. That source lists only mixtures and none of the pure נוקשה items. This shows רבי אליעזר does not prohibit נוקשה. The משנה does count נוקשה as forbidden, so it cannot follow רבי אליעזר, just as רב יהודה said.

keyTerms.meaning: 'Whom have you heard say...' — identifies which תנא holds a certain view
Learn from it — the proof is accepted
He does not hold of it

steps.whatToRemember: According to רבי אליעזר, real חמץ gets כרת and its mixture gets a לאו. Pure נוקשה is not prohibited at all. This is why רב יהודה attributes the משנה to רבי מאיר and not to רבי אליעזר.
steps.whyThisMatters: This removes the basis for רב נחמן's קל וחומר. A stricter rule for mixtures does not automatically carry over to pure נוקשה.

phrases.english: Whom have you heard
who says that for its mixture there is a lav?
It is Rabbi Eliezer,
whereas pure hardened chametz it does not mention.
Learn from this:
Rabbi Eliezer does not hold of a prohibition on hardened chametz.

steps.triggerLanguage: מַאן שָׁמְעַתְּ לֵיהּ דְּאָמַר עַל עֵירוּבוֹ בְּלָאו
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Draws the conclusion from the ברייתא quoted in Step 24
steps.maskanaFinalTakeaway: The ברייתא follows רבי אליעזר. Since it omits pure נוקשה, רבי אליעזר does not prohibit נוקשה, which supports רב יהודה.

steps.title: Where does רבי אליעזר get a לאו for a mixture?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks for the source of רבי אליעזר's ruling that a mixture of חמץ carries a לאו.
steps.simpleTranslation: And רבי אליעזר — where does he learn that a mixture of חמץ carries a לאו?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא asks for the source of רבי אליעזר's rule. The answer comes in the next step.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Now that we know רבי אליעזר's position, the גמרא wants its scriptural root. It is not challenging him, only asking for his source.

keyTerms.meaning: From where does he learn it?
A Torah prohibition (lighter than כרת)

phrases.english: And Rabbi Eliezer,
from where does he learn that its mixture carries a lav?

steps.triggerLanguage: וְרַבִּי אֱלִיעֶזֶר, עֵירוּבוֹ בְּלָאו מְנָא לֵיהּ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Moves from identifying רבי אליעזר's view to asking for its source
steps.sheelahInformationSought: The פסוק that is the source for רבי אליעזר's לאו on a mixture of חמץ

steps.title: The source: You shall eat nothing leavened
steps.stepSummary: רבי אליעזר learns the לאו for a mixture from the פסוק 'כל מחמצת לא תאכלו'.
steps.simpleTranslation: As it is written: 'You shall eat nothing leavened.'
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers that רבי אליעזר's source is the פסוק 'כל מחמצת לא תאכלו'.
steps.deeperAnalysis: This is the same פסוק the ברייתא in Step 24 used to include the four mixed foods. The broad wording 'anything leavened' reaches beyond plain חמץ to cover its mixture as well, with a לאו.

keyTerms.meaning: As it is written
Something leavened

phrases.english: As it is written:
"You shall eat nothing leavened."

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the question of Step 26
steps.sheelahInformationSought: The source for a לאו on a mixture

steps.title: Then a mixture should also get כרת
steps.stepSummary: If 'מחמצת' includes a mixture of חמץ, the כרת verse also says 'מחמצת', so a mixture should carry כרת as well.
steps.simpleTranslation: If so, he should also make a person liable to כרת, because it is written: 'For anyone who eats מחמצת will be cut off.'
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא challenges the source it just gave for רבי אליעזר. The same word appears in a verse about כרת.
steps.deeperAnalysis: If the word 'מחמצת' brings in a mixture for the לאו, the same word in the כרת verse should bring in a mixture for כרת. But the ברייתא in Step 24 said a mixture gets only a לאו, not כרת. So the word cannot be what includes a mixture.

keyTerms.meaning: If so (if your logic is correct)
The punishment of being 'cut off', given for knowingly eating real חמץ on פסח
Something leavened
And it will be cut off

steps.confusionAlert: There are two different verses with the word 'מחמצת'. One is the לאו verse, 'כל מחמצת לא תאכלו'. The other is the כרת verse, 'כי כל אוכל מחמצת ונכרתה'. Keep track of which verse is being discussed.

phrases.english: If so, let him also make one liable to karet,
since it is written:
"For whoever eats anything leavened shall be cut off"!

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Attacks the source given in Step 27
steps.kashyaTarget: The derivation of a לאו for a mixture from the word 'מחמצת'
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: The same word appears in the כרת verse. If it includes a mixture there too, a mixture would get כרת, which goes against the ברייתא.

steps.title: The כרת verse teaches about food leavened by something else
steps.stepSummary: The word 'מחמצת' in the כרת verse is needed for a different teaching: כרת applies even to food that became חמץ because of an outside agent.
steps.simpleTranslation: That word is needed for what was taught in a ברייתא: From 'מחמצת' I only know about food that became חמץ by itself. How do I know about food that became חמץ because of something else? The verse says: 'Anyone… מחמצת will be cut off.'
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers that the word 'מחמצת' in the כרת verse is already being used for something else. So it is not available to teach about mixtures.
steps.deeperAnalysis: A ברייתא uses the כרת verse to teach that dough which became חמץ because of an outside agent still counts as full חמץ for כרת. Since the word is used up on that teaching, it does not also include mixtures. That is why a mixture gets no כרת.

keyTerms.meaning: He needs it (for a different teaching)
It became חמץ by itself
Because of something else (an outside agent)
The verse teaches

phrases.english: He needs that verse
for that which was taught in a baraita:
("Leavened") I only have food that became leavened on its own;
from where do I know food leavened due to something else?
The verse states: "Anything… leavened… shall be cut off."

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the challenge of Step 28
steps.terutzResolutionType: The verse is needed for a different teaching
steps.terutzHavaAmina: 'מחמצת' in the כרת verse includes a mixture, so a mixture gets כרת
steps.terutzMaskana: 'מחמצת' in the כרת verse teaches that food leavened by an outside agent gets כרת. It does not teach about a mixture.

steps.title: Then the לאו verse should teach the same thing
steps.stepSummary: If 'מחמצת' means food leavened by an outside agent, then the same word in the לאו verse should mean that too, and not a mixture.
steps.simpleTranslation: If so, the לאו verse should also come for this same teaching!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא turns the answer around. If 'מחמצת' means food leavened by something else, it should mean that in the לאו verse as well.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The two verses use the same word, so the word should mean the same thing in both. Then 'כל מחמצת לא תאכלו' teaches only about food leavened by an outside agent. It would give no source at all for a לאו on a mixture.

keyTerms.meaning: A negative commandment (a 'do not' prohibition)
It comes for this purpose

phrases.english: If so,
the verse of the prohibition also comes for this purpose!

steps.triggerLanguage: אִי הָכִי, דְּלָאו נָמֵי לְהָכִי הוּא דַּאֲתָא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Uses the answer of Step 29 to undo the source given in Step 27
steps.kashyaTarget: Using 'מחמצת' in the לאו verse as the source for a mixture
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: The same word should mean the same thing in both verses. So the לאו verse is also about food leavened by an outside agent, and there is no source left for a mixture.

steps.title: רבי אליעזר learns the mixture from the word 'כל'
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא changes the source: רבי אליעזר learns the לאו for a mixture from the word 'כל' (anything), not from 'מחמצת'.
steps.simpleTranslation: Rather, the reason of רבי אליעזר comes from the word 'כל'.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא gives up the earlier source and gives a new one. רבי אליעזר's לאו for a mixture comes from the word 'כל' in 'כל מחמצת לא תאכלו'.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Both verses use 'מחמצת' for food leavened by an outside agent. The extra word 'כל' (anything) is what widens the לאו to include a mixture of חמץ. This solves both problems: a mixture gets a לאו, and the word 'מחמצת' means the same thing in both verses.

keyTerms.meaning: Rather (we take back the earlier answer)
The reason, or source
'Anything', a word that includes more cases

steps.whatToRemember: For רבי אליעזר, the word 'מחמצת' teaches that food leavened by an outside agent is real חמץ. The word 'כל' in the לאו verse adds a לאו for a mixture of חמץ. A mixture never gets כרת.
steps.whyThisMatters: This sets the final source for רבי אליעזר's view on mixtures of חמץ. That view was the basis for Steps 23–25 about whether he also forbids נוקשה.

phrases.english: Rather: the reason of Rabbi Eliezer is from the word "anything."

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Replaces the source of Step 27 after the challenge in Step 30
steps.terutzResolutionType: A new source replaces the old one
steps.terutzHavaAmina: The לאו for a mixture comes from the word 'מחמצת'
steps.terutzMaskana: The לאו for a mixture comes from the word 'כל'

steps.title: The כרת verse also says 'כל'
steps.stepSummary: If 'כל' in the לאו verse includes a mixture, then 'כל' in the כרת verse should also include a mixture, which would mean a mixture carries כרת.
steps.simpleTranslation: There too, isn't it written 'כל'?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא attacks the answer it just gave. The word 'כל' also appears in the verse that gives כרת for eating חמץ.
steps.deeperAnalysis: In Step 31, the source for the mixture לאו was moved to the word 'כל'. But the כרת verse ('כי כל אוכל מחמצת ונכרתה') also has the word 'כל'. If 'כל' includes a mixture, it should include a mixture for כרת too, yet רבי אליעזר holds that a mixture carries only a לאו.

keyTerms.meaning: There (here: in the כרת verse)
Also, too
Isn't it written?
All, anything, whoever

phrases.english: There too,
phrases.notes: Refers to the כרת verse: 'כי כל אוכל מחמצת ונכרתה'.

phrases.english: isn't it written 'all/whoever'?
phrases.notes: So by the same reasoning, a mixture should carry כרת.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges the new source ('כל') proposed in Step 31.
steps.kashyaTarget: The claim that 'כל' in the לאו verse teaches a mixture.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: The same word appears in the כרת verse. If it includes a mixture there as well, a mixture would carry כרת, which contradicts רבי אליעזר's view that it carries only a לאו.

steps.title: 'כל' in the כרת verse includes women
steps.stepSummary: The word 'כל' in the כרת verse is needed for a different teaching: that women are also punished with כרת for eating חמץ.
steps.simpleTranslation: That word is needed to include women.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers that 'כל' in the כרת verse is already used for something else, so it cannot also teach a mixture.
steps.deeperAnalysis: A word in the Torah that is needed for one teaching is not free to teach a second one. 'כל' in the כרת verse is used to include women in the punishment of כרת. Only 'כל' in the לאו verse is free, so only the לאו covers a mixture.

keyTerms.meaning: He needs it (for a different teaching)
To include
Women

phrases.english: That one he needs
phrases.notes: The word 'כל' in the כרת verse, according to רבי אליעזר.

phrases.english: to include women.
phrases.notes: Women also get כרת for eating חמץ.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the challenge of Step 32.
steps.terutzResolutionType: The word is needed for another teaching (מיבעי ליה).
steps.terutzHavaAmina: 'כל' in the כרת verse is free to include a mixture.
steps.terutzMaskana: 'כל' in the כרת verse is used to include women, so it does not teach a mixture.

steps.title: Women are already included by a general rule
steps.stepSummary: There is no need for 'כל' to include women, since a general rule already makes men and women equal for all Torah punishments.
steps.simpleTranslation: Women can be learned from what רב יהודה said in the name of רב. For רב יהודה said in the name of רב, and the school of רבי ישמעאל taught the same: The verse says, 'A man or woman, when they commit any of the sins of men.' The Torah made a man equal to a woman for all punishments in the Torah.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא attacks the last answer. It says women are already covered by a general rule, so 'כל' should not be needed for them.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The verse 'איש או אשה כי יעשו מכל חטאת האדם' teaches that men and women are equal for every punishment in the Torah. כרת for eating חמץ is one of those punishments. So 'כל' seems unnecessary for women, and it should again be free to include a mixture.

keyTerms.meaning: It is derived, it comes out
A teaching from the school of רבי ישמעאל
The verse made equal
Punishments

steps.whyThisMatters: This is the general source that women are obligated in all the Torah's prohibitions and their punishments.

phrases.aramaic: נָשִׁים מִדְּרַב יְהוּדָה אָמַר רַב נָפְקָא,
phrases.english: Women are derived from what Rav Yehuda said in the name of Rav,
for Rav Yehuda said in the name of Rav,
and so too the school of Rabbi Yishmael taught:
The verse says: 'A man or a woman
when they commit any of the sins of men,'
the verse made a man equal to a woman
for all the punishments in the Torah.

steps.triggerLanguage: נָשִׁים מִדְּרַב יְהוּדָה אָמַר רַב נָפְקָא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges the answer of Step 33 by showing that its teaching is already known from elsewhere.
steps.kashyaTarget: The claim that 'כל' in the כרת verse is needed to include women.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: A general verse already makes women equal to men for all punishments, so 'כל' is unnecessary for women and should be free to teach a mixture.

steps.title: A special source for women is still needed
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא begins its answer: a specific source for women regarding חמץ is still necessary. The reason comes on the next amud.
steps.simpleTranslation: It is necessary,
steps.whatsHappening: This step sets up the next move. The גמרא states that a separate source for women is still needed, and it is about to explain why.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The general rule might not have been enough in the case of חמץ, because of a special reason the גמרא gives on the next amud. If so, 'כל' is truly needed to include women, and the answer from Step 33 holds.

keyTerms.meaning: It was necessary

steps.confusionAlert: This step does not end here. 'איצטריך' only opens the answer. The reason why the general rule is not enough continues on the next amud.

phrases.english: It is necessary,
phrases.notes: The explanation of why continues on the next amud.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Begins answering the challenge of Step 34 and defends Step 33.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Necessity (איצטריך): the general rule is not enough in this specific case.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: The general verse equating men and women already covers חמץ.
steps.terutzMaskana: A specific inclusion of women for חמץ is still needed, for a reason explained next.
